record.original_question: Determine whether a mechanism analogous to the proposed chamber-and-damper apparatus can explain cascades in real hydrodynamics, and whether one can choose the parameters n_i, m_i, and r_i so that the model functions as intended, ideally with an analogue in two-dimensional ideal fluid flow.

evidence.quote: Problem 40. Is there a similar mechanism which describes a cascade in real hydrodynamics? Is it possible to define the parameters ni , mi , and ri in such a way that the above apparatus works as intended? It would be interesting and important to find a link between this device and a more convenient heat engine; in particular, to find some analogues of Maxwell’s demon or, perhaps even more importantly, to show that a similar mechanism works in a 2D ideal fluid, thus ensuring inverse energy cascade in it.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following idealized mechanical "chamber-and-damper" apparatus intended to model an energy cascade. The device consists of a finite collection of coupled chambers, indexed by i, each equipped with three positive real parameters: an integer mode number n_i (interpreted as a characteristic wavenumber or number of internal degrees of freedom), a mass parameter m_i, and a damping (or coupling) coefficient r_i. The dynamics among the chambers are designed so that energy injected at one scale is transferred, through the chain of couplings, toward chambers with smaller n_i (a large-scale, or "inverse," cascade), in a manner formally analogous to inverse energy cascade phenomena.

(a) Determine whether a mechanism of this type can be made to faithfully describe energy cascades occurring in real (viscous, three-dimensional) hydrodynamics.

(b) Decide whether one can explicitly choose the parameters {n_i}, {m_i}, {r_i} so that the apparatus actually exhibits the intended cascade behavior, and exhibit such a choice if it exists.

(c) Establish a rigorous link between such a mechanical device and a heat-engine-type model, in particular constructing an analogue of Maxwell's demon within this framework.

(d) Most importantly, construct an analogue of this mechanism within the dynamics of a two-dimensional ideal (Euler) incompressible fluid on a bounded domain or torus, and use it to give a mathematically rigorous mechanism producing inverse energy cascade in 2D ideal hydrodynamics.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent open problem list concerning mechanical/Hamiltonian models of cascades in 2D hydrodynamics. No published resolution providing a rigorous mechanism for inverse energy cascade in the 2D Euler equation along these lines has been located; the question is generally regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Problems on mechanical models of cascades (arXiv:2205.01143)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem list including a question on whether a chamber-and-damper mechanism explains cascades in real hydrodynamics and admits a 2D ideal-fluid analogue.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as open in a recent problem collection.
